tags.name: Aquarium
tags.notes: Located in Mirbat area, Dhofar region. Site type corrected from 'wall' to 'reef' in prior pass: multiple sources describe this as a coral garden/reef with large table corals, not a vertical wall. Shore-accessible via Mirbat's boat operators, shallow coral garden 8-18m. Seasonal: Oct-May. RE-AUDIT 2026-08-16 (HALLUCINATION FOUND AND CORRECTED): the marine-life text in the prior markdown pass ("hundreds of shrimp gobies", "some of the largest moray eels in the region") was traced to bluewaterdivetravel.com's description of a DIFFERENT site also named "Aquarium" located in the Hallaniyat Islands ("Aquarium, Hallaniyat... Only visited once each week by one liveaboard") -- a remote offshore location, not this Mirbat shore site. That species list has been removed from the markdown as a source misattribution. Replacement marine-life text now draws on offbeatenwaves.com/divesalalah-aggregated descriptions of the Mirbat trio (Eagle Bay, China Wreck, Aquarium) collectively: nudibranchs, flatworms, shrimp and other crustaceans, clownfish, octopus, morays, and stonefish, with rays, turtles and barracudas also reported in the area -- phrased as cluster-level, not asserted as Aquarium-exclusive sightings.

tags.name: China Wreck (direction 150deg)
tags.notes: Located in Mirbat area, Dhofar region. Direction '150deg' is a navigational bearing from shore. Seasonal: Oct-May. WRECK-HISTORY DEEP RESEARCH 2026-08-16 (per deep-QA requirement, >=2 independent sources cross-checked; no Wikipedia article exists for this vessel under either spelling -- searched and confirmed absent): Oman Observer (2021, https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1103793/oman/tourism/oman-completes-documentation-of-sunken-ship-kiva) and Muscat Daily (2021, https://www.muscatdaily.com/2021/07/13/ministry-completes-documenting-128-year-old-wreckage-off-mirbat/) both report Oman's Ministry of Heritage and Tourism documented a '128-year-old' wreck off Mirbat identified as the 'Kiva' -- a pilgrim vessel that departed Bombay for Mecca in 1893 with ~979 pilgrims, lost to a cargo-hold fire. SOURCE CONFLICT: separate tour-booking sources (GetYourGuide, Expedia, and syndicated reprints) describe a 'Kheva Wreck' that sank in 1874 after a fire en route from Bombay to Jeddah, resting in only 3-5 metres of water shallow enough for snorkellers. 'Kiva' and 'Kheva' are widely treated online as the same vessel (name variant), but the sinking year (1893 vs 1874), destination (Mecca vs Jeddah), and critically the DEPTH (this dive site is a 25m boat-accessible wreck vs the 3-5m snorkel-depth 'Kheva Wreck' tourism product) directly conflict. This may indicate two distinct wrecks conflated under similar names, or a single debris field spanning shallow-to-deep sections. No primary maritime database (Lloyd's Register, Wrecksite.eu) entry was located to resolve this -- searched, none found. One Salalah operator source describes the site only as 'a former steam-powered vessel scattered over ~80m N-S' without naming the Kiva, and the 'China Wreck' name may alternatively reflect porcelain/china cargo found among the debris rather than the ship's origin. Vessel identity, exact build date, tonnage, and precise sinking date remain UNVERIFIED beyond 'probable Kiva/Kheva, fire-related loss, Bombay-departure pilgrim vessel, late 19th century.' Do not state any of the conflicting specifics (year, destination, depth) as settled fact -- markdown must present them as a conflict.

Flagged unresolved: <3 substantive sources found despite renewed search (WebSearch for "ABT Salalah" wreck dive site, dive.site, divescover.com, dive.site profile of ABT Divers all reviewed -- none name a distinct 'ABT Salalah' wreck). Wreck identity and site-specific facts remain unresolved; validated flag left unchanged per instruction not to downgrade solely for source count, since the existing description already honestly discloses the unknowns rather than fabricating them.

tags.name: Eagle Bay
tags.notes: Located in Mirbat area, Dhofar region, ~70km from Salalah. Site type corrected from 'wreck' to 'reef' in prior pass. Features sandy patch, coral bank (south), rocky outcrops (north). Depth 5-15m. Beginner-friendly, minimal currents. Seasonal: Oct-May. RE-AUDIT 2026-08-16: original SSI/divessi.com dive-guide link (mydiveguide/divesite/60130) now returns a 301 redirect to a generic scubago.com homepage with no site-specific content -- dropped as a dead source. Replaced with PADI's dedicated Eagle Bay (Oman) dive-site page, which corroborates depth (5-15m) and adds confirmed species. MARINE-LIFE CORRECTION: prior markdown text claimed 'large batfish and boxfish also commonly reported' -- this is not corroborated by any current source (GetYourGuide or PADI) and has been removed. Corrected/expanded species list per GetYourGuide + PADI: turtles, rays, honeycomb moray eels, sharks, starfish, groupers, Moorish idols, anemonefish.

tags.name: Dibba Rock Reef
tags.notes: Located at Dibba, northern Musandam Peninsula, Oman side of the UAE/Oman border. Coordinates confirmed in Oman (not UAE). Rocky reef with walls, caves, and drop-offs. Suitable for beginners though currents can be present during tidal changes. Accessible from both UAE and Oman side operators. Protected marine area. RE-AUDIT 2026-08-16: the SSI/divessi.com dive-guide link (mydiveguide/divesite/99470) that previously supported the '40m per SSI guide' depth claim now also returns a 301 redirect to a generic scubago.com homepage -- dead source, dropped. DEPTH CONFLICT flagged: re-researched across divers-guide.com (dedicated dive-site database with logged dives: reports 7-15m as the working range) versus other aggregator listings citing drop-offs to 30-40m; these do not agree, and the most detailed primary dive-log source caps it near 15m. Markdown now presents this as a range/conflict rather than asserting 40m as settled fact. Reef shark sighting corroborated by two independent sources: visitmusandam.com ('occasional reef sharks') and divers-guide.com (gray reef shark and blacktip reef shark specifically logged).

tags.name: Snoopy Island Reef
tags.notes: GEOGRAPHIC ISSUE (unresolved, carried forward): coordinates place this site at ~25.49N, 56.36E -- Al Aqah, Fujairah, UAE, NOT Oman. OSM placed this under Oman in error; jurisdiction is actually UAE/Fujairah. Not corrected in this pass (out of scope -- would require removing the site from the Oman destination file, which the deep-QA task did not request; flagged for a future data-integrity pass). At 24m depth, corresponds to 'Snoopy Deep Reef' (also 'New Reef'), an artificial reef built around a purposely-sunk dive boat and trailer, ~500m east of the shallow Snoopy Island itself. WRECK-HISTORY NOTE: this is a modern purpose-sunk artificial reef, not a historic wreck with a ship name/build date/tonnage/sinking-cause to cross-check -- no fabricated history has been added, consistent with anti-hallucination policy. RE-AUDIT 2026-08-16: dropped nemodivingcenter.com from validation_source -- re-checked and its Snoopy Island guide covers only the shallow Snoopy Island itself and lists Dibba Rock/Martini Rock/Inchcape 1 Wreck as alternatives; it does not mention Snoopy Deep Reef/New Reef at all and does not substantively support this site. Replaced with medium.com (Reef Oasis Diving Center), which directly confirms Snoopy Deep Reef specifics: ~24m depth, angelfish, boxfish, snapper schools, wrasse, moray eels, seahorses -- consistent with coralcreekdiving.com. Minor DEPTH CONFLICT flagged: PADI's dedicated page states 26m (85ft) while Coral Creek and Reef Oasis both state ~24m; markdown now notes the 24-26m range rather than picking one figure. MARINE-LIFE NOTE: PADI's community-sourced species list additionally includes 'sharks, whales, dolphins, turtles' -- broader/vaguer than the two dive-shop sources and not corroborated by either; retained only as a caveated 'occasionally reported' note rather than presented as typical sightings, since whales at a 24-26m artificial reef would be an atypical, unverified claim.
